## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭhamaaniyata* ("First Undetermined Rule", Bu-Vb Ay1) constitutes the opening rule of the *Aniyata* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates cases where a trustworthy female lay disciple witnesses a monk sitting privately with a woman in a secluded, concealed location suitable for sexual intercourse. If she accuses the monk of an offense entailing expulsion (*pārājika*), formal suspension (*saṅghādisesa*), or confession (*pācittiya*), and the monk admits to having committed the act, he is adjudicated according to whichever of the three classes of offense he acknowledges. The text includes the canonical framing narrative, the formulation of the training rule, and the word commentary (*padabhājaniya*), translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
